Provided that RevMed is permitted to conduct a RevMed Study, RevMed shall report to the JRDC on an ongoing basis any and all data arising from a RevMed Study (the \"RevMed Study Data\") and provide the JRDC with updates and any other information pertaining to any RevMed Study as may be requested by the JRDC."},{"id":"p0328","text":"A. Sanofi shall have rights to use, at no additional cost, any RevMed Study Data in its performance of its obligations and exercise of its rights under the Collaboration except in connection with filing of MAAs for the Indication and Product Treatment Regimen that were the subject of such RevMed Study."},{"id":"p0329","text":"B. If Sanofi wishes to use, or actually uses, RevMed Study Data in support of filing a MAA for the Indication and Product Treatment Regimen that were the subject of such RevMed Study, it shall notify RevMed in writing and shall make a buy-in payment to RevMed in Dollars equal to [***] within [***] after the date that Sanofi receives a detailed invoice from RevMed setting forth [***]. In such case the RevMed Study shall be deemed a Clinical Trial under the Collaboration for all purposes, including that all Know-How conceived, reduced to practice, developed, made or otherwise generated by or on behalf of RevMed or its Affiliates in the course of the RevMed Study activities shall be deemed Program Inventions hereunder."},{"id":"p0330","text":"C. Each Party shall have rights to use RevMed Study Data for internal research and development outside the scope of the Collaboration."},{"id":"p0331","text":"5.7 Diligence. Consistent with [***] or as otherwise agreed by the Parties, Sanofi shall use Commercially Reasonable Efforts [***] to file and seek approval for an MAA for at least one Product in all of such countries or, in the case of the Major Market Countries in the European Union, through the centralized European Union approval process. If Sanofi materially breaches its obligation set forth in this Section 5.7, [***]."},{"id":"p0332","text":"5.8 Development Records. Each Party shall maintain complete, current and accurate records of all Development activities conducted by it hereunder, and all data and other information resulting from such activities, for at least [***] after the expiration or termination of this Agreement in its entirety or for such longer period as may be required by Applicable Law. Such records shall fully and properly reflect all work done and results achieved in the performance of the Development activities in good scientific manner appropriate for regulatory and patent purposes. Each Party shall document all non-clinical studies and Clinical Trials for Products in formal written study reports in accordance with Applicable Law and national and international guidelines (e.g., GCP, GLP, and GMP). Each Party shall have the right to review and copy such records maintained by the other Party at reasonable times and to obtain access to the original to the extent necessary for regulatory and patent purposes or for other legal proceedings."},{"id":"p0333","text":"5.9 Data Exchange and Development Reports. In addition to adverse event and safety data reporting obligations pursuant to Section 6.5, each Party shall promptly provide the other Party with copies of all data and results generated by or on behalf of such Party in the course of performing the Development activities hereunder, including, in each case of data arising from 37"},{"id":"p0334","text":"Clinical Trials for Products, or in such form as the JRDC may agree from time to time. Each Party shall provide the JRDC with regular reports detailing its Development activities for the Products, and the results of such activities at each regularly scheduled JRDC meeting. The Parties shall discuss the status, progress and results of each Party's Development activities at such JRDC meetings."},{"id":"p0335","text":"5.10 Clinical Samples. The Party who sponsors the applicable Clinical Trial of SHP2 Inhibitors shall retain and archive all clinical samples obtained by such Party in the course of such Clinical Trial, and shall provide the other Party reasonable access to such retained clinical samples."},{"id":"p0336","text":"Article VI."}]}

RevMed will also have the right to notify Sanofi in writing if RevMed believes a Milestone Event has been achieved even if Sanofi has not provided such notice to RevMed, and unless Sanofi notifies RevMed within [***] Business Days after receipt of such notice from RevMed that such Milestone Event has not been achieved, RevMed may issue an invoice to Sanofi for the corresponding Milestone Payment. Subject to the other terms of this Section 9.3, during the Royalty Term, Sanofi shall make quarterly royalty payments to RevMed on aggregate Net Sales of each Product sold outside the United States during a Calendar Year at the applicable royalty rates as set forth below. For clarity, royalties shall only be payable once on any sale of Product under this Agreement."},{"id":"p0394","text":"Aggregate Net Sales of each Product outside the United States during a Calendar Year Royalty Rate Portion of aggregate Net Sales of each Product outside the United States during a Calendar Year less than or equal to $[***] [***]% Portion of aggregate Net Sales of each Product outside the United States during a Calendar Year greater than $[***] and less than or equal to $[***] [***]% Portion of aggregate Net Sales of each Product outside the United States during a Calendar Year greater than $[***] and less than $[***] [***]% Portion of aggregate Net Sales of each Product outside the United States during a Calendar Year greater than $[***] [***]% 45"},{"id":"p0395","text":"(b) Royalty Term. Sanofi's royalty payment obligations under this Section 9.3 with respect to a particular Product and country shall commence upon the First Commercial Sale of such Product in such country (by Sanofi or its Affiliates or Sublicensees) and shall continue, on a Product-by-Product and country-by-country basis, until the latest of (i) the date on which there is no Valid Claim that would be infringed by the sale of such Product in such country; (ii) the expiration of any Regulatory Exclusivity granted with respect to such Product in such country[***] (the \"Royalty Term\" for such Product and country)."},{"id":"p0396","text":"(c) Royalty Reductions."},{"id":"p0397","text":"(i) In any country in which there is no Valid Claim and no Regulatory Exclusivity for such Product, at the time of sale of such Product in such country during the applicable Royalty Term, Sanofi's obligation to pay royalties under Section 9.3(a) on Net Sales of such Product in such country shall be reduced to [***]% of the rates otherwise payable under such section."},{"id":"p0398","text":"(ii) If during the Royalty Term for a Product in a country, one or more Generic Products of such Product are sold in such country, and during any Calendar Quarter following the Calendar Quarter in which such Generic Product(s) are first sold in such country (the \"Launch Quarter\") Net Sales of such Product in such country during any Calendar Quarter following the Launch Quarter are less than the Designated Percentage (as defined below) of average Net Sales occurring during the [***] immediately preceding the Launch Quarter (such average Net Sales during such Calendar Quarters, the \"Base Net Sales\"), then the royalty rates provided in Section 9.3(a) for such Product shall be reduced in such country by the \"Applicable Reduction Percentage\" set forth below for such Calendar Quarter and for all future Calendar Quarters, unless and until the Generic Product is no longer sold or the Net Sales increase above the Base Net Sales in a Calendar Quarter. If Net Sales of the applicable Product in a country in a Calendar Quarter following the Launch Quarter for such country are:"},{"id":"p0399","text":"A. lower than or equal to [***]%, but more than [***]%, of Base Net Sales of the applicable Product in such country, then the Applicable Reduction Percentage shall be [***]%; or"},{"id":"p0400","text":"B. lower than or equal to [***]% of Base Net Sales of the applicable Product in such country, then the Applicable Reduction Percentage shall be [***]%."},{"id":"p0401","text":"(iii) If Sanofi enters into an agreement with a Third Party in order to obtain a license or other right to a Third Party Right that is reasonably necessary to manufacture, use or sell a Product (or the SHP2 Inhibitor contained therein) in a country pursuant to Section 10.7, Sanofi shall be entitled to deduct from the royalties payable under Section 9.3(a) with respect to such Product in such country in a particular Calendar Quarter [***] paid by Sanofi to such Third Party in respect of such agreement for such Calendar Quarter, in each case to the extent reasonably allocable to such Third Party Right and such Product and country; provided that in no event shall the royalties payable for such Product and country in any Calendar Quarter be reduced to less than [***]% of the amount otherwise due under Section 9.3(a) (the \"Royalty Floor\"). If any of such amounts cannot be offset against royalties due with respect to a Product for any Calendar Quarter because they would result in royalties payable to RevMed being lower than the Royalty Floor, Sanofi shall have 46"},{"id":"p0402","text":"the right to carry forward and offset such excess amount against royalties or any other payments otherwise due to RevMed in subsequent Calendar Quarters up to a maximum reduction for each Quarter of [***]% of the amounts owed in respect of such subsequent Calendar Quarter. Upon RevMed's written request Sanofi shall provide a summary to RevMed with respect to the scope of the licensed rights and payments due pursuant to such Third Party license, provided that RevMed may only make such a request one time for each Third Party license."},{"id":"p0403","text":"(d) Royalty Reports and Payment."},{"id":"p0404","text":"(i) Within [***] after each Calendar Quarter, commencing with the Calendar Quarter during which the First Commercial Sale of the first Product is made anywhere in the Licensed Territory, Sanofi shall provide RevMed with a report that contains the following information for the applicable Calendar Quarter:"},{"id":"p0405","text":"(i) on a country-by-country and Product-by-Product basis, the amount of Net Sales of the Products (which may be provided in Dollars or Euros), (ii) on a country-by-country basis and on a Product-by-Product basis, a calculation of the royalty payment due on such sales, and (iii) the exchange rate for such country. Within [***] following delivery of the applicable quarterly report, Sanofi shall pay in Dollars all royalties due to RevMed with respect to Net Sales by Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective Sublicensees for such Calendar Quarter."},{"id":"p0406","text":"(ii) Within [***] after each Calendar Year, commencing with the Calendar Year during which the First Commercial Sale of the first Product is made anywhere in the Licensed Territory, Sanofi shall provide RevMed with [***]."},{"id":"p0407","text":"(e) Clarifications. For the purpose of calculating the aggregate Net Sales of a particular Product for an applicable country to determine the applicable royalty rate under Section 9.3, all Products containing the same SHP2 Inhibitor shall be deemed a single Product, regardless of form, formulation, dosage, packaging, other active ingredient or component, label or intended patient population. All royalty payments under this Section 9.3 are non-refundable and non-creditable."},{"id":"p0408","text":"9.4 U.S. Profit/Loss Share. No later than the Initiation of the first Registrational Clinical Trial for the first Product, Sanofi and RevMed shall enter into a profit/loss share agreement (the \"Profit/Loss Share Agreement\") pursuant to which the Parties shall equally share the Net Profit and Net Loss (as defined in Exhibit M of the Correspondence) applicable with respect to Commercialization of Products (but, for clarity, not any costs of Development) of Products in the U.S. The Profit/Loss Share Agreement for a Product in the U.S. shall continue in effect until the expiration of the Royalty Term for such Product in the U.S. and shall contain the terms and conditions set forth in Exhibit M of the Correspondence and other terms and conditions as are reasonable and customary for the sharing of profits and losses with respect to similar products in the United States (including that each Party shall bear its own income taxes, that each Party is entitled to withhold any tax on behalf of the other Party on payments made to the other Party as required by Applicable Law (taking into account any legally available reduction or elimination of such tax pursuant to an applicable tax treaty or otherwise), and each Party shall indemnify the other Party with respect to any withholding taxes asserted or assessed by any taxing authority on amounts received directly by, or deemed allocable to, such other Party. 47"},{"id":"p0409","text":"9.5 Payment Terms; Exchange Rate. Notwithstanding any term to the contrary of this Agreement, RevMed shall deliver an invoice to Sanofi for all payments owed by Sanofi to RevMed under this Agreement. Sanofi will make all payments owed to RevMed within [***] after the date on which Sanofi receives an undisputed invoice for such owed amount, except where a different timeframe is expressly provided in another Section of this Agreement (e.g., for the reimbursement of RevMed R&D Costs pursuant to Sections 4.5 and 5.5; the payment of the buy-in payment pursuant to Section 5.6(b)B; the upfront payment set forth in Section 9.1; the royalties payable pursuant to Section 9.3, the payment of VAT pursuant to Section 9.7(b); and the payment of unpaid or overpaid amounts pursuant to Section 9.9(b)). All payments to be made by a Party to the other Party under this Agreement shall be made in Dollars by bank wire transfer in immediately available funds to a bank account designated by written notice from the Party that receives the payment. Conversion of Net Sales or reimbursable costs incurred hereunder that are recorded in local currencies to Dollars by a Party, its Affiliates or its or their Sublicensees shall be performed in a manner consistent with its normal practices used to prepare its audited financial statements for internal and external reporting purposes."},{"id":"p0410","text":"9.6 Late Payments. If a Party does not receive payment of any undisputed sum due to it on or before the due date therefor, then it shall notify the paying Party. The paying Party shall pay interest on any undisputed late payments (before and after any judgment) at an annual rate (but with interest accruing on a daily basis) of the lesser of (a) [***] percent above the London Interbank Offered Rate for deposits in Dollars having a maturity of one month published by the British Bankers' Association, as adjusted from time to time on the [***] of each month, such interest to run from the date on which payment of such sum became due until payment thereof in full together with such interest or (b) the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law."},{"id":"p0411","text":"9.7 Taxes."},{"id":"p0412","text":"(a) General. Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all income taxes imposed on its share of income arising directly or indirectly from the activities of the Parties under this Agreement. In the event that Sanofi is required, under Applicable Law, to withhold any deduction or tax from any payment due to RevMed under this Agreement (taking into account any legally available reduction or elimination of such tax pursuant to an applicable tax treaty or otherwise), such amount will be deducted from the payment to be made by Sanofi, paid to the proper taxing authority, and Sanofi will notify RevMed and upon RevMed's request promptly provide RevMed with copies of any tax certificate or other documentation evidencing such withholding, provided, however, that in the event that any such withholding tax arises as a result of Sanofi's re-domiciliation, assignment of its rights or obligations hereunder to an Affiliate, or use of any Third Party subcontractor, payments to RevMed hereunder shall be made on a grossed-up basis to ensure that RevMed receives the same amount it would have in the absence of such withholding. Each Party agrees to cooperate with the other Party in claiming exemptions from such deductions or withholdings under any agreement or treaty from time to time in effect."},{"id":"p0413","text":"(b) Value Added Tax. Notwithstanding anything contained in Section 9.7(a), this Section 9.7(b) will apply with respect to value added tax (or sales, use or indirect tax) (\"VAT\"). All payments to be made by Sanofi hereunder are exclusive of VAT. If any VAT is chargeable in respect of any such payments, Sanofi will notify RevMed and pay VAT at the applicable rate in respect of any such payments following the receipt of a VAT invoice in the appropriate form issued by RevMed in respect of those payments or Sanofi shall self-assess and pay such VAT, such VAT to be payable on the later of the due date of the payment to which such VAT relates and [***] after the receipt by Sanofi of the applicable invoice relating to that VAT payment. 48"},{"id":"p0414","text":"9.8 Records. Each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Sublicensees to, maintain complete and accurate financial books and records in sufficient detail to permit the other Party to confirm the accuracy of the amount of amounts payable under this Agreement. Each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Sublicensees to, retain such books and records until the later of (a) [***] after the end of the period to which such books and records pertain and (b) the expiration of the applicable tax statute of limitations (or any extensions thereof) or for such longer period as may be required by Applicable Law."},{"id":"p0415","text":"9.9 Audit Procedures."},{"id":"p0416","text":"(a) Upon reasonable prior notice of the other Party, but in any event at least [***] prior notice, each Party shall and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Sublicensees to permit an independent auditor of international prominence, selected by the auditing Party and reasonably acceptable to the audited Party, to audit the books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8 for the sole purpose of verifying for the auditing Party the accuracy of the financial reports furnished by the audited Party pursuant to this Agreement or of any payments made, or required to be made, by or to the audited Party pursuant to this Agreement or any Ancillary Agreement. Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause, and shall not concern books and records relating to a period more than [***] preceding the current Calendar Year. Any failure by a Party to exercise its rights under this Section 9.9 with respect to a Calendar Year within such [***] period shall constitute a waiver by such Party of its right to later object to any payments made by the other Party under this Agreement during such Calendar Year."},{"id":"p0417","text":"(b) Upon completion of the audit, the auditor shall provide a report to both Parties, which report shall be limited to a description of any failure to comply with the terms of this Agreement and the amount of the financial discrepancy. Such auditor shall not disclose the audited Party's Confidential Information to the auditing Party, except to the extent such disclosure is necessary to verify the accuracy of the financial reports furnished by the audited Party or the amount of payments to or by the audited Party under this Agreement. Any amounts shown to be owed but unpaid, or overpaid and in need of reimbursement, shall be paid or refunded (as the case may be) within [***] after the auditor's report, plus interest (as set forth in Section 9.6) from the original due date (unless challenged in good faith by the audited Party in which case any dispute with respect thereto shall be resolved in accordance with Section 15.6)."},{"id":"p0418","text":"(c) The auditing Party shall bear the full cost of such audit unless such audit reveals an underpayment by the audited Party that resulted from a discrepancy in the financial report provided by the audited Party for the audited period, which underpayment was more than [***] percent of the amount set forth in such report, in which case the audited Party shall reimburse the auditing Party for the costs for such audit."},{"id":"p0419","text":"(d) The auditing Party shall treat all information subject to review under this Section 9.9 in accordance with the confidentiality provisions of Article XI and the Parties shall cause the auditor to enter into a reasonably acceptable confidentiality agreement with the audited Party obligating such auditor to retain all such financial information in confidence pursuant to such confidentiality agreement. 49"},{"id":"p0420","text":"Article X."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ COMMERCIALIZATION","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0362","text":"COMMERCIALIZATION"},{"id":"p0363","text":"8.1 General. Subject to Section 8.7 and unless otherwise delegated to RevMed by the JCC, Sanofi shall have the sole right and responsibility, at its own expense, for all aspects of the Commercialization of the Products in the Field in the Licensed Territory including:"},{"id":"p0364","text":"(a) developing and executing a commercial launch and pre-launch plan, (b) negotiating with applicable Governmental Authorities regarding the pricing and reimbursement status of the Products;"},{"id":"p0365","text":"(c) marketing and promotion (including promotional materials);"},{"id":"p0366","text":"(d) booking sales and distribution and performance of related services;"},{"id":"p0367","text":"(e) handling all aspects of order processing, invoicing and collection, inventory and receivables;"},{"id":"p0368","text":"(f) providing customer support, including handling medical queries, and performing other related functions; and (g) conforming its practices and procedures to Applicable Law relating to the marketing, detailing and promotion of the Products."},{"id":"p0369","text":"8.2 Commercialization Plan. Promptly after the formation of the JCC, Sanofi shall prepare and provide to the JCC for review and discussion a written plan for the Commercialization of such Product in the Licensed Territory (the \"Commercialization Plan\"). Each Commercialization Plan shall include a reasonably detailed description of (a) [***];"},{"id":"p0370","text":"(e) non-binding sales and marketing forecasts in the U.S.;"},{"id":"p0371","text":"(f) non-binding net sales projections in the U.S.;"},{"id":"p0372","text":"(g) [***];"},{"id":"p0373","text":"(h) non-binding sales and marketing forecasts and non-binding net sales projections, in each case, outside of the U.S."},{"id":"p0374","text":"(i) [***], and in such case the Parties shall amend the Profit/Loss Share Agreement accordingly. Sanofi shall periodically (at least [***]) prepare updates and amendments to its Commercialization Plan to reflect changes in its plans, including in response to changes in the marketplace, relative success of the Products and other relevant factors influencing such plans and activities. Sanofi shall submit all updates and amendments to each Commercialization Plan to the JCC for review and discussion before adopting such updates and amendments."},{"id":"p0375","text":"8.3 Distributorships. Sanofi shall have the right, in its sole discretion, to appoint its Affiliates, and Sanofi and its Affiliates shall have the right, in its sole discretion, to appoint any other Persons, in the Licensed Territory to distribute, market, and sell the Products (with or without packaging rights), in circumstances where the Person purchases its requirements of Products from Sanofi or its Affiliates but does not otherwise make any royalty or other payment to Sanofi or its Affiliates with respect to its intellectual property or other proprietary rights. Where Sanofi or its Affiliates appoints such a Person and such Person is not an Affiliate of Sanofi, that Person shall be a \"Distributor\" for purposes of this Agreement. The term \"packaging rights\" in this Section means the right for the Distributor to package Products supplied in unpackaged bulk form into individual ready-for-sale packs."},{"id":"p0376","text":"8.4 Pricing Approvals. Sanofi shall control all pricing and reimbursement approvals for Products in the Licensed Territory. RevMed shall provide Sanofi with reasonable assistance and cooperation with respect to obtaining pricing and reimbursement approvals for the Products, at Sanofi's request and expense. 42"},{"id":"p0377","text":"8.5 Patent Marking. input.quote: (i) Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall payment or volume cap on us. Searches for "minimum", "shortfall", "take or pay" and "commit to purchase" return nothing relevant. Article VII (Manufacturing and Supply) contemplates a future Supply Agreement with price at [***] but sets no committed volumes (p0360); the Commercialization Plan forecasts and net sales projections are expressly "non-binding" (p0370, p0371, p0373). Our financial obligations are usage/activity-based: reimbursement of actual RevMed R&D Costs incurred per an agreed Budget (capped at a stated percentage of budgeted amounts), one-time milestone payments on achievement (capped at $520,000,000), and royalties on Net Sales. In addition, Sanofi holds a broad termination-for-convenience right in its entirety or on a country/Product basis (p0488), so even the funding commitments are exitable. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only); no redline required. We note only that Sanofi carries Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence obligations (§5.7) and cost-share percentages for 2019-2020, which are effort/cost-sharing terms rather than volume or spend commitments and are addressed under other rules.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Aventis, Inc. (Sanofi); counterparty is Revolution Medicines, Inc. (RevMed).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Research and Development Costs shall initially be borne by the Party incurring the cost or expense."},{"id":"p0300","text":"Promptly following the end of each Calendar Quarter during Calendar Years 2019 and 2020, but in no event later than [***] following the end of such Calendar Quarter, each Party will provide to the JRDC a detailed expense report in form approved by the JRDC with respect to the Research and Development Costs incurred by or on behalf of such Party during such Calendar Quarter consistent with the previous sentence (including, if requested by Sanofi in writing, copies of receipts or invoices from Third Parties for all RevMed R&D Out-of-Pocket Costs). [{"id":"p0484","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"TERM AND TERMINATION"},{"id":"p0485","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"12.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence upon the Effective Date and, unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Article XII, shall continue in full force and effect until the expiration of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement, whichever is later (the \"Term\")."},{"id":"p0486","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"12.2 Termination."},{"id":"p0487","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"(a) Terminations by Sanofi."},{"id":"p0488","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"(i) Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed; provided that if Sanofi desires to terminate this Agreement under this Section 12.2(a)(i)B only with respect to the U.S. (for all Products or one or more Products), Sanofi shall provide [***] written notice of termination to RevMed."},{"id":"p0489","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"(ii) For a Change of Control of RevMed. RevMed will notify Sanofi in writing as soon as possible after RevMed announces publicly any information regarding any proposed Change of Control of RevMed (or if the Change of Control will not be publicly announced, then no later than [***] after the signing of the Change of Control). Sanofi will have the option to either (A) terminate this Agreement in its entirety upon written notice to RevMed provided to RevMed within [***] of the effective date of such Change of Control; or (B) [***]."},{"id":"p0490","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"(iii) For Safety. Sanofi will have the right to terminate this Agreement in its entirety or on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis, upon [***] prior written notice to RevMed, due to safety concerns raised by a Regulatory Authority, an Institutional Review Board for a Clinical Trial or by Sanofi's internal regulatory decision makers acting in accordance with Sanofi's standard internal policies (any such entity or group, a \"Safety Reviewer\"), where such Safety Reviewer recommends cessation of Development or Commercialization of such SHP2 Inhibitor or Product with respect to any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product (and a summary of such concerns will be stated in the notice of termination). During such [***] notice period, each Party will continue to perform all of its obligations under this Agreement then in effect. 58"},{"id":"p0491","sectionRef":"§ TERM AND TERMINATION","text":"(b) Termination for Material Breach. If either Party believes that the other is in material breach of this Agreement, then the non-breaching Party may deliver notice of such breach to the other Party. For all material breaches other than a failure to make a payment as set forth in this Agreement, the allegedly breaching Party shall have [***] from such notice to dispute or cure such breach. For any material breach arising from a failure to make a payment set forth in this Agreement, the allegedly breaching Party shall have [***] from the receipt of the notice to dispute or cure such breach. If the Party receiving notice of material breach under this Agreement fails to cure, or fails to dispute, such breach within the applicable time period set forth above, then the Party originally delivering the notice of material breach may terminate this Agreement effective on written notice of termination to the other Party. If the allegedly breaching Party in good faith disputes such material breach or disputes the failure to cure or remedy such material breach and provides written notice of that dispute to the other Party within the applicable period set forth above, the matter shall be addressed under the dispute resolution provisions in Section 15.6. During the pendency of any such dispute, all of the terms and conditions of this Agreement will remain in effect and the Parties will continue to perform all of their respective obligations hereunder."}]

{"sectionRef":"§ DEVELOPMENT","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0303","text":"DEVELOPMENT"},{"id":"p0304","text":"5.1 General. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Parties will collaborate on the Development of the Products in the Field for Regulatory Approval under the direction of the JRDC and pursuant to the Development Plan, as set forth in more detail below."},{"id":"p0305","text":"5.2 Development."},{"id":"p0306","text":"(a) Development Plan and Budget. As of the Effective Date, the Parties have agreed on an initial Development Plan and Development Budget (each as defined below), which is set forth in Exhibit J of the Correspondence. After the Effective Date, for the Development Candidate listed in Exhibit J of the Correspondence, and at the time any other SHP2 Inhibitor is designated as a Development Candidate by the JRDC, the JRDC shall prepare and approve a Development plan for Products containing such SHP2 Inhibitor through Regulatory Approval of the Product from the FDA, EMA, or PMDA, as applicable, that includes the items described below (the \"Development Plan\"). The Development Plan for each Product shall set forth the timeline and details of:"},{"id":"p0307","text":"(i) all clinical Development activities to be conducted by the Parties that are designed to generate data sufficient to present to the FDA, EMA, and PMDA or other Regulatory Authority at the Pre-Registrational Meetings;"},{"id":"p0308","text":"(ii) the protocol synopsis for each Clinical Trial included in such Development Plan;"},{"id":"p0309","text":"(iii) a Manufacturing plan for the Manufacturing of the Product for such Clinical Trials;"},{"id":"p0310","text":"(iv) all additional clinical Development activities to be conducted by the Parties that are designed to generate data sufficient to seek Regulatory Approval of the Product from the FDA, EMA, or PMDA, as applicable, for the indication(s) to be pursued;"},{"id":"p0311","text":"(v) any other Development activities to be performed in order to obtain Regulatory Approval by the FDA, EMA, PMDA or the Regulatory Authority of any other jurisdiction;"},{"id":"p0312","text":"(vi) a detailed budget setting forth the estimated RevMed R&D Costs to be incurred in connection with such activities (the \"Development Budget\"); and (vi) the Party responsible for conducting each Development activity under such Development Plan. 34"},{"id":"p0313","text":"(b) Conduct of Development. Each Party shall perform all Development activities under this Agreement in compliance with all Applicable Law (including GMP, GLP and GCP). In furtherance and not in limitation of the foregoing, RevMed shall use diligent efforts to conduct its activities under each Development Plan in accordance with the terms of such Development Plan (including timelines), as the same may be amended from time to time (and which basis for comparison shall be tolled until any then-contemplated or pending amendments are completed or for the duration of any bona fide dispute between the Parties with respect to a Development Plan or amendment thereto), and this Agreement."},{"id":"p0314","text":"If either RevMed agrees or it is determined in accordance with [***] that RevMed has committed a material breach of its obligations under this Section 5.2(b) with respect to any Clinical Trial of a Product, the JSC shall, within [***] after such agreement on or determination of material breach, meet in person or by teleconference to discuss such material breach and specify reasonable actions that RevMed should take to cure such material breach. If RevMed fails to commence within [***] after such discussion occurs such actions recommended by the JSC, or fails to cure any such material breach within [***] after the JSC meets (or such longer timeframe as the JSC decides is necessary to complete the actions specified by the JSC), then Sanofi shall have the right, without prejudice to any other rights or remedies Sanofi may have under this Agreement or otherwise at law or in equity[***]."},{"id":"p0315","text":"In such case, RevMed shall, [***], (i) make available [***], (ii) provide [***], (iii) provide [***], and (iv) otherwise provide [***]."},{"id":"p0316","text":"(c) Pre-Registrational Meeting. After obtaining early Development data and results under the Development Plan for a particular Product, in the event the JRDC determines to further Develop such Product for Marketing Approval, the JRDC shall develop a package setting forth such data and results, a planned regulatory strategy for the Development of such Product for a defined indication in the Field, the protocol synopses for each Registrational Clinical Trial included in the applicable Registration Program, any other Development activities to be conducted in support of such regulatory strategy, any other materials as may be required by the FDA, EMA, or PMDA or other Regulatory Authority for the Pre-Registrational Meetings for the applicable Products, and the Party responsible for conducting each Development activity under such package (the \"Data Package\"). After developing such Data Package, the Parties shall conduct the Pre-Registrational Meetings as set forth in Section 6.3(a)."},{"id":"p0317","text":"(d) Development Plan Amendments. From time to time during the Term, the JRDC shall prepare amendments, as appropriate, to the then-current Development Plan. Subject to the foregoing, the JRDC shall have the right to approve amendments to the Development Plan, with final decision-making authority as provided in Section 2.10. Once approved by the JRDC, such amended Development Plan shall replace the prior Development Plan."},{"id":"p0318","text":"5.3 Combination Therapies."},{"id":"p0319","text":"(a) The JRDC shall discuss whether to include in the Development Plan for a Product the Development of such Product for use with other products to the extent not already provided for in the Development Plan (each, a \"Combination Therapy\"), including products developed or sold by a Third Party or that are in the public domain. Subject to this Section 5.3, each Party shall have the right to propose to the JRDC studies for co-development of Products with other products under the applicable Development Plan. 35"},{"id":"p0320","text":"(b) The Development Plan shall address the conduct of any Clinical Trial for a Combination Therapy and shall (i) specify which Party will be responsible for each activity for the Development of such Combination Therapy and (ii) specify which Party will be responsible for obtaining supplies of the Product or other product in such Combination Therapy as necessary. The JRDC shall review and approve the terms of any agreement with a Third Party in connection with any supply or other aspect of Development of such Combination Therapy."},{"id":"p0321","text":"5.4 Conflicts. If the terms of a Development Plan contradict, or create inconsistencies or ambiguities with, the terms of this Agreement, then the terms of this Agreement shall govern."},{"id":"p0322","text":"5.5 Development Costs."},{"id":"p0323","text":"(a) Sanofi will reimburse RevMed for RevMed R&D Costs incurred by or on behalf of RevMed after the Execution Date in the performance of its activities under the Development Plan, as applicable, provided that such RevMed R&D Costs are incurred per the Development Budget, as applicable, for such activities as approved by the JSC and do not exceed [***]% of the applicable amounts set forth in the Development Budget for the particular Calendar Quarter. Promptly following the end of each Calendar Quarter during which RevMed is responsible for activities under any Development Plan, but in no event later than [***] following the end of such Calendar Quarter, RevMed will provide to Sanofi a detailed expense report in form approved by the JRDC with respect to the RevMed R&D Costs incurred by or on behalf of RevMed during such Calendar Quarter consistent with the previous sentence (including, if requested by Sanofi in writing, copies of receipts or invoices from Third Parties for all RevMed Out-of-Pocket Costs) together with an invoice for the same, provided that [***]. Sanofi will reimburse RevMed in Dollars all undisputed amounts within such expense reports under this Section 5.5 within [***] following receipt of the invoice therefor. RevMed shall invoice Sanofi for costs under this Section 5.5 on an accrual basis."},{"id":"p0324","text":"5.6 RevMed Studies."},{"id":"p0325","text":"(a) RevMed or its Affiliates may propose to the JRDC that the Parties conduct a Clinical Trial of a Product in the Field that is not included in the Development Plan for such Product, in which case RevMed shall present the proposed design and projected costs of such Clinical Trial to the JRDC. If Sanofi agrees to include such Clinical Trial and related costs in the Development Plan and Development Budget for such Product, the Parties shall prepare an updated Development Plan and Development Budget and such Clinical Trial shall become part of the Collaboration and subject to this Agreement."},{"id":"p0326","text":"(b) In the event Sanofi, through the JRDC, decides not to pursue a Clinical Trial that RevMed presents in accordance with Section 5.6(a), then (i) the matter will be escalated pursuant to Section 2.10 and (ii) notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section 2.10(b), if such matter remains unresolved after the matter is escalated to Designated Senior Officers, then RevMed, subject to this Section 5.6(b), may elect to conduct such study, on its own and at its own expense, provided that if such study [***], RevMed shall not have the right to conduct such study unless Sanofi agrees in writing that RevMed may conduct such study (any such study so conducted, a \"RevMed Study\"). For purposes of determining whether subsections (x), (y) or (z) apply, RevMed shall, prior to commencing a RevMed Study, submit to the JRDC for comment and review 36"},{"id":"p0327","text":"the protocol for such RevMed Study. Any disagreement among the JRDC members as to whether subsections (x), (y) or (z) apply shall be submitted for resolution to the Designated Senior Officers, provided that if the Designated Senior Officers do not agree on such matter, then RevMed shall not conduct such study. Provided that RevMed is permitted to conduct a RevMed Study, RevMed shall report to the JRDC on an ongoing basis any and all data arising from a RevMed Study (the \"RevMed Study Data\") and provide the JRDC with updates and any other information pertaining to any RevMed Study as may be requested by the JRDC."},{"id":"p0328","text":"A. Sanofi shall have rights to use, at no additional cost, any RevMed Study Data in its performance of its obligations and exercise of its rights under the Collaboration except in connection with filing of MAAs for the Indication and Product Treatment Regimen that were the subject of such RevMed Study."},{"id":"p0329","text":"B. If Sanofi wishes to use, or actually uses, RevMed Study Data in support of filing a MAA for the Indication and Product Treatment Regimen that were the subject of such RevMed Study, it shall notify RevMed in writing and shall make a buy-in payment to RevMed in Dollars equal to [***] within [***] after the date that Sanofi receives a detailed invoice from RevMed setting forth [***]. In such case the RevMed Study shall be deemed a Clinical Trial under the Collaboration for all purposes, including that all Know-How conceived, reduced to practice, developed, made or otherwise generated by or on behalf of RevMed or its Affiliates in the course of the RevMed Study activities shall be deemed Program Inventions hereunder."},{"id":"p0330","text":"C. Each Party shall have rights to use RevMed Study Data for internal research and development outside the scope of the Collaboration."},{"id":"p0331","text":"5.7 Diligence. Consistent with [***] or as otherwise agreed by the Parties, Sanofi shall use Commercially Reasonable Efforts [***] to file and seek approval for an MAA for at least one Product in all of such countries or, in the case of the Major Market Countries in the European Union, through the centralized European Union approval process. If Sanofi materially breaches its obligation set forth in this Section 5.7, [***]."},{"id":"p0332","text":"5.8 Development Records. Each Party shall maintain complete, current and accurate records of all Development activities conducted by it hereunder, and all data and other information resulting from such activities, for at least [***] after the expiration or termination of this Agreement in its entirety or for such longer period as may be required by Applicable Law. Such records shall fully and properly reflect all work done and results achieved in the performance of the Development activities in good scientific manner appropriate for regulatory and patent purposes. Each Party shall document all non-clinical studies and Clinical Trials for Products in formal written study reports in accordance with Applicable Law and national and international guidelines (e.g., GCP, GLP, and GMP). Each Party shall have the right to review and copy such records maintained by the other Party at reasonable times and to obtain access to the original to the extent necessary for regulatory and patent purposes or for other legal proceedings."},{"id":"p0333","text":"5.9 Data Exchange and Development Reports. In addition to adverse event and safety data reporting obligations pursuant to Section 6.5, each Party shall promptly provide the other Party with copies of all data and results generated by or on behalf of such Party in the course of performing the Development activities hereunder, including, in each case of data arising from 37"},{"id":"p0334","text":"Clinical Trials for Products, or in such form as the JRDC may agree from time to time. Each Party shall provide the JRDC with regular reports detailing its Development activities for the Products, and the results of such activities at each regularly scheduled JRDC meeting. The Parties shall discuss the status, progress and results of each Party's Development activities at such JRDC meetings."},{"id":"p0335","text":"5.10 Clinical Samples. The Party who sponsors the applicable Clinical Trial of SHP2 Inhibitors shall retain and archive all clinical samples obtained by such Party in the course of such Clinical Trial, and shall provide the other Party reasonable access to such retained clinical samples."},{"id":"p0336","text":"Article VI."}]}

Sanofi's royalty payment obligations under this Section 9.3 with respect to a particular Product and country shall commence upon the First Commercial Sale of such Product in such country (by Sanofi or its Affiliates or Sublicensees) and shall continue, on a Product-by-Product and country-by-country basis, until the latest of (i) the date on which there is no Valid Claim that would be infringed by the sale of such Product in such country; content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer)

The agreement contains no take-or-pay analogue running against us:

- **No minimum volumes.** Article VII contemplates a future Supply Agreement at a defined transfer price, but sets no committed quantities or shortfall mechanic (§7.3).
- **Forecasts are expressly non-binding.** The Commercialization Plan's sales/marketing forecasts and net sales projections are labelled "non-binding" both for the U.S. and ex-U.S. (§8.2).
- **Payments are activity- and outcome-based.** Reimbursement of actual RevMed R&D Costs incurred per an approved Budget (with a percentage overrun cap), one-time milestones on achievement (aggregate capped at $520M), and royalties on Net Sales — i.e., fees for work performed or sales made, not for unused capacity.
- **Exit exists in any event.** Sanofi has termination for convenience in its entirety or on a country-by-country/Product-by-Product basis, which exceeds the fallback's reducibility requirement.

This sits at the **preferred** position, so no redline was proposed. Noted for the record but not flagged: Sanofi's Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence obligation (§5.7) and the 80/20 cost-share for Calendar Years 2019–2020 are effort and cost-sharing terms rather than volume or spend commitments, and belong to other rules.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-2b68bb7e","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION; LIABILITY; INSURANCE","rationale":"Section 14.1 gives us a RevMed indemnity for (a) RevMed's negligence/recklessness/willful misconduct, (b) breach of its representations and warranties, and (c) breach of its obligations, with standard notice, control and cooperation procedure in Section 14.3, and Section 14.5 confirms the consequential-damages waiver does not cut back indemnities. However, it contains no head of indemnity for third-party claims that the licensed technology or the Products infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. That risk is only picked up indirectly through breach of the Article XIII IP warranties, most of which are knowledge-qualified and given only as of the Execution Date (p0549: \"To RevMed's Knowledge... does not infringe\"), while Section 14.2(a) affirmatively places third-party claims arising from our Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products on us, and Section 10.7 only gives us a first right to negotiate a third-party licence at our own cost. Under the detection guidance this fails the fallback (Vendor indemnity excluding IP infringement), so we propose the minimal addition of an express IP infringement head as new Section 14.1(d), leaving RevMed's existing carve-outs for our own negligence and breaches intact. Our own indemnity in Section 14.2 is otherwise appropriately confined to our development/commercialization conduct and breaches.","proposal":"Add a RevMed third-party IP infringement indemnity to Section 14.1","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-60daf895","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS","rationale":"The IP architecture protects Sanofi and creates no prohibited transfer to RevMed. Section 10.1(a) requires each Party to obtain assignment of Program Inventions from its own Third Parties to that Party (and Section 3.4 requires subcontractor assignment, or failing that an irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, exclusive, royalty-free worldwide licence with sublicensing rights to the engaging Party), so work generated for Sanofi vests in Sanofi; \"Sanofi Sole Program Know-How\"/\"Sanofi Sole Program Patents\" (1.109-1.110) confirm Sanofi solely owns its own Program Inventions and Section 10.4(c) gives Sanofi sole enforcement of them. Joint Program Technology is jointly owned but each Party may exploit and license it with no duty of accounting and no consent, backed by a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable cross-licence — i.e. joint ownership with an unrestricted right to exploit, which sits at the fallback rather than the \"no joint ownership\" preferred position and is therefore acceptable. Sanofi's data and regulatory position are preserved and enhanced: RevMed assigns all Regulatory Approvals (INDs/NDAs) to Sanofi (6.2), transfers the global safety database at its own cost (6.5), and Sanofi owns all Product Marks and domain names (10.5). There is no assignment of Sanofi background IP or Sanofi Sole Program Technology to RevMed: Section 3.2 is only a narrow non-exclusive, royalty-free sublicence back of RevMed's own licensed technology solely to let RevMed perform its obligations, and Section 3.6 negates implied licences. The Article XII reversion is a bargained-for, licence-based unwind limited to Termination Products, triggered largely by Sanofi's own convenience/change-of-control election or Sanofi default, and carries post-termination royalties payable to Sanofi (12.3(c)(ii)C). Noted but not flagged: the ownership allocation in 10.1(a) is redacted [***], so the sole/joint split is inferred from the defined terms; if the unredacted text allocated Sanofi-generated inventions to RevMed we would revisit.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-71b0bce3","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION; LIABILITY; INSURANCE","rationale":"Section 14.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision in the Agreement (searches for \"aggregate liability\" and other cap language return nothing else, and Section 14.6 expressly says insurance does not create a liability limit). It is mutual and waives indirect/consequential damages and lost profits, and it preserves the indemnities under Sections 14.1-14.2, confidentiality (Article XI) and IP (Article X) outside that waiver — all consistent with the playbook's carve-out expectations. However, there is no monetary cap of any kind: both Parties' direct-damages exposure is unlimited. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least twelve months' fees. As the paying party facing uncapped direct-damages claims (for example for alleged breach of diligence or of Article XIV obligations), a mutual cap is materially in our interest. Redline inserts a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, keeps the existing indemnity/confidentiality/IP carve-outs plus gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud outside the cap, and confirms Sanofi's payment obligations are not \"damages\" for cap purposes.","proposal":"Add a mutual aggregate liability cap to Section 14.5, with indemnification, confidentiality, IP, gross negligence/willful misconduct/fraud and Sanofi's payment obligations outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-2b30fcb7","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Section 15.2 substantially meets our preferred position. Sanofi may assign to any Affiliate without RevMed's consent (15.2(a)(i)) and may assign in whole, without consent, to a successor or purchaser in a sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction (15.2(a)(ii)) - the full affiliate/M&A carve-out. RevMed, by contrast, needs Sanofi's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments, and may not assign or transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without Sanofi's consent (15.2(b)). Critically, no RevMed right is triggered by a Sanofi Change of Control: RevMed's termination rights (12.2(b)-(e): material breach, insolvency, Sanofi Competing Product, cessation of activity) contain no change-of-control trigger, and there is no vendor exit or re-pricing on our change of control during the term. Two points noted but not flagged: (1) RevMed may assign in whole on its own Change of Control without our consent, short of the preferred \"consent / never to a competitor\" formulation, but mitigated by RevMed's advance notice obligation and our option to terminate (or elect the 12.2(a)(ii)B alternative) on a RevMed Change of Control, plus the firewall conditions in 15.2 (separateness of Competing Product activities, no Know-How exchange, Acquiror Family IP excluded) - this sits at or above the mutual-successor-assignment fallback; (2) the post-termination royalty payable to us under 12.3(c) ends on a Change of Control of Sanofi, and 9.7(a) allocates to us the withholding gross-up arising from a Sanofi affiliate assignment - minor sub-elements of separate financial terms rather than assignment restrictions. No redline required.</rationale>\n</invoke>\n","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-fd3b708b","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"LICENSE","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Sanofi, so it meets the preferred position. All exclusivity runs in our favour: Section 3.1 grants Sanofi an exclusive licence (even as to RevMed) and an exclusive option, and Section 13.2(q) is a RevMed warranty that no third-party exclusivity limits our rights. On sourcing, Article VII gives Sanofi oversight of Registrational/commercial Manufacture, requires RevMed to transfer Manufacturing Know-How on request and to support Sanofi in establishing its own third-party supply agreements (Section 7.2); Section 7.3 only requires good-faith negotiation of a Supply Agreement where one Party in fact manufactures for the other, with no requirements/sole-source commitment. Noted but not flagged: Section 12.2(d) gives RevMed a termination right if Sanofi develops a Competing Product without having commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product, subject to a Sanofi election to cure — that is a conditional termination right rather than an exclusive-dealing covenant restricting our freedom to source or develop, and it is standard in a collaboration of this type. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-60b269c4","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"FINANCIAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty or minimum-fee provision payable by Sanofi (our party). Searches for \"liquidated damages\" and \"penalty\" return nothing; the financial provisions (Article IX) impose only upfront, milestone, royalty and profit/loss-share payments tied to actual performance, and the sole late-payment consequence is ordinary reciprocal interest at LIBOR + [***]% capped at the maximum lawful rate (Section 9.6), which the rule expressly treats as not a liquidated-damages deviation. Termination by Sanofi for convenience under Section 12.2(a)(i) requires only notice, with no early-termination or minimum fee; the post-termination royalty flow in Section 12.3(c)(ii)C runs from RevMed to Sanofi and so benefits us. For diligence failures under Section 5.7, Section 12.6 makes termination the exception to the \"not sole remedy\" rule rather than imposing a fixed sum. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-30a9c59b","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"LICENSE","rationale":"The grant to us (Section 3.1(a), p0248) is exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), covers the full value chain in the \"Field\" (defined as \"any and all uses\") and the \"Licensed Territory\" (all countries and territories of the world), and is not revocable at RevMed's discretion — RevMed can terminate only for uncured material breach (p0491), insolvency (p0492) or the negotiated Competing Product / cessation-of-activity triggers (p0493, p0495), each with notice and cure. Affiliate and contractor coverage sits at the preferred position: Section 3.4(a) lets us exercise rights and perform obligations through any Affiliate without RevMed's consent, Section 3.4(b) permits sublicensing through multiple tiers (only a U.S. \"substantially all\" sublicense needs consent that cannot be unreasonably withheld), and Section 3.4(c)(i) lets us subcontract to Third Parties as we deem appropriate. Section 15.2(a)(ii) permits assignment without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all related assets, merger or acquisition, satisfying the transferability requirement. Only drafting nuance: Affiliate/contractor rights live in Section 3.4 rather than in the grant language itself, and the U.S. mega-sublicense consent and Acquiror-Family carve-outs (p0612) are mild frictions — noted, not material deviations.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-cdf324ca","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"needs_review","rationale":"Worker failed and requires manual review: Tool loop exceeded 12 iterations","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-t4c-b9cda566","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Section 12.2(a)(i) gives Sanofi (our party) an at-will termination right, exercisable both in its entirety and on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis, with no early-termination fee or penalty attached; Section 12.3(c) sets out only wind-down/transition consequences, and Section 12.3(c)(ii)C in fact requires RevMed to pay Sanofi post-termination royalties on Termination Products, which runs in our favour. RevMed has no reciprocal convenience right: its termination rights are limited to cause-based triggers (12.2(b) material breach, 12.2(c) insolvency, 12.2(d) Sanofi Competing Product, and 12.2(e) cessation of development, each with notice, meet-and-discuss and cure mechanics). That matches the preferred position (Customer convenience right; no Vendor convenience right during the Term). The notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted ([***]), so the exact length cannot be confirmed from the document; we should verify on the execution version that the entirety notice is workable and note that the preferred 30-day standard is unusual for a collaboration of this type. That open sub-element is noted rather than flagged.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-501279f1","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"FINANCIAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Section 9.9 is the only provision giving RevMed audit rights over Sanofi's payment records (the Article VI audit right at p0354 runs in our favour, against RevMed, so is not flagged). It is mutual and contains every material element of the preferred position: capped frequency (no more than [***] per Calendar Year), advance written notice, access only via an independent auditor of international prominence that must be reasonably acceptable to us and must sign a confidentiality agreement (9.9(d)), a report limited to describing non-compliance and the discrepancy amount with no disclosure of our other Confidential Information (9.9(b)), a look-back window tied to the retention period in 9.8, and cost borne by the auditing Party unless an underpayment exceeds a stated percentage threshold (9.9(c)). There is no right of direct or remote access to Customer systems and no unannounced or unlimited audit right, so walk-away territory is not engaged. The specific numerals for notice, frequency and the underpayment percentage are redacted ([***]), so we cannot confirm whether they hit the preferred 30 days/5% or sit at the fallback 15 days/10%; these figures should be confirmed against the unredacted execution copy. The \"unless for cause\" carve-out to the frequency cap is a minor sub-element short of the preferred wording and, given the clause is fully reciprocal, does not warrant a redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-e479f6e3","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Governing law is New York law (Section 15.5, and the same for the side Letter at p0671), which matches our preferred position. The dispute forum is arbitration rather than New York County courts, but it is not foreign arbitration: it is administered by JAMS under its Comprehensive Arbitration Rules and Procedures with proceedings in English, patent/trademark scope and validity disputes are carved out to the courts of the granting country (15.6(h)), Program Invention ownership goes to U.S. patent counsel under U.S. patent law (15.6(i)), and either Party may seek interim or equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction (15.6(j)). That is well outside walk-away territory (vendor home-jurisdiction law or arbitration seated abroad) and satisfies the rule on its material terms. Two sub-points noted rather than flagged: the arbitral seat and number of arbitrators in 15.6(a) are redacted ([***]), so we should confirm on turn that the seat is in the United States (ideally New York, New York), and 15.6(f) bars punitive/exemplary damages in arbitration — a mutual limitation that does not disadvantage us asymmetrically.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-d2857331","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","rationale":"We swept the document for MFN-style language (\"no less favourable\"/\"no less favorable\", \"most favored nation\", \"more favorable\", \"comparable terms\", \"match\") and found none. The FINANCIAL PROVISIONS article (upfront, milestones, royalty rates and reductions, Royalty Floor, U.S. profit/loss share) and the MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY article contain only fixed, negotiated economics; supply pricing under Section 7.3 is set by a specified formula rather than by reference to terms granted to third parties. Sanofi therefore has no obligation to extend RevMed terms no less favourable than those given to any third party or to match third-party offers, which meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer). No redline is warranted; a Vendor-granted MFN would also be acceptable but none exists here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-e8fd874b","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","rationale":"The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall payment or volume cap on us. Searches for \"minimum\", \"shortfall\", \"take or pay\" and \"commit to purchase\" return nothing relevant. Article VII (Manufacturing and Supply) contemplates a future Supply Agreement with price at [***] but sets no committed volumes (p0360); the Commercialization Plan forecasts and net sales projections are expressly \"non-binding\" (p0370, p0371, p0373). Our financial obligations are usage/activity-based: reimbursement of actual RevMed R&D Costs incurred per an agreed Budget (capped at a stated percentage of budgeted amounts), one-time milestone payments on achievement (capped at $520,000,000), and royalties on Net Sales. In addition, Sanofi holds a broad termination-for-convenience right in its entirety or on a country/Product basis (p0488), so even the funding commitments are exitable. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only); no redline required. We note only that Sanofi carries Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence obligations (§5.7) and cost-share percentages for 2019-2020, which are effort/cost-sharing terms rather than volume or spend commitments and are addressed under other rules.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-c7538552","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"hire\", \"induce\", \"employ or engage\" and a full read of the GENERAL PROVISIONS article (sec-p0605) and the representations/covenants articles turned up no non-solicitation, no-hire or employee-inducement covenant; the only hits for \"solicited\"/\"employee\" relate to committee input, FTE definitions, confidentiality recipients, debarment covenants and indemnitee definitions. The integration clause confirms the Agreement is the entire understanding, so no non-solicit binds Sanofi from a superseded instrument (the prior Confidentiality Agreement is expressly superseded). This matches our preferred position of no non-solicit on the Customer, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-c8a6b078","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"This is a collaboration/license agreement with a single fixed Term that runs until expiry of Sanofi's payment obligations; there is no automatic renewal, no renewal term, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price-uplift mechanic (searches for \"renew\"/\"automatically renew\"/successive-term language return only unrelated patent, insurance and force majeure references). Any extension would therefore require mutual written agreement, which matches the preferred position, and Sanofi additionally holds broad termination-for-convenience rights under Section 12.2(a)(i). The auto-renewal rule is effectively not applicable, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-caac2f11","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIALITY; PUBLICATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains a full exit/transition architecture, so no clause is missing. Section 11.6 gives a mutual, on-request return/destruction-with-written-certification mechanic for Confidential Information (with reasonable archival/back-up carve-outs), which is the data-return element the rule seeks and is not an immediate-deletion walk-away. Section 12.3 sets out detailed wind-down mechanics: transfer of Regulatory Approvals, Regulatory Materials, clinical and pharmacovigilance data within fixed periods (12.3(c)(iv), (d)(iii)), a defined Transition Assistance package including technical assistance and Know-How transfer for a stated post-termination period (12.3(c)(vi)C), inventory sell-off and transition services (12.3(c)(iii), (vi)G), and RevMed-side assistance to Sanofi on a Change of Control termination (12.3(e)); Section 7.2 obliges RevMed to transfer Manufacturing Know-How to Sanofi on request. Direction is structurally reversed from a typical hosting deal: because rights in the Products revert to RevMed on termination, most transition duties properly run from Sanofi to RevMed, so those obligations are the bargained reversion consideration rather than a rule breach and we do not flag them. Noted but not flagged: the durations are redacted ([***]) so we cannot confirm a 90-day/6-month floor, and Section 7.2 is not listed in the Section 12.4 survival list, so post-expiry manufacturing know-how support is not expressly preserved. Overall the clause set meets or exceeds the fallback position.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-17d85e41","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.3 Covenants by RevMed. RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:","rationale":"This is a drug research/development and commercialization collaboration, not a services or software purchase, so the rule's parameters map onto RevMed's performance standards and warranty package rather than a fixed software/deliverable conformance period. The material protections the rule targets are all present and sit at or above the fallback:\n\n1. Performance standard (the \"professional and workmanlike\" analogue): Section 4.2(b) (p0291) and Section 5.2(b) (p0313) require RevMed to perform all Research and Development activities \"in compliance with all Applicable Law (including GMP, GLP and GCP)\" and to use diligent efforts to conduct activities in accordance with each Research/Development Plan, including timelines. GMP/GLP/GCP is the industry-standard equivalent of the preferred workmanlike/industry-standards covenant.\n\n2. Real remedy: Sections 4.2(b) and 5.2(b) give a graduated cure mechanic (JRDC/JSC-specified cure actions, cure periods) followed by Sanofi step-in/transfer rights \"without prejudice to any other rights or remedies Sanofi may have under this Agreement or otherwise at law or in equity\" (p0292, p0314). Re-performance and cure are therefore backed by full retained remedies, plus RevMed indemnifies Sanofi for material breach of its warranties (p0583) and material breach supports termination. This is a stronger remedy than the rule's repair/replace/refund floor.\n\n3. Compliance with laws: warranted at Section 13.2(u) (p0564) and covenanted mutually at Section 13.4(b) (p0572).\n\n4.
